purpose: Record GitHub/GitHub Actions as PR/publication/shadow evidence adapters while Prow/Kubernetes-native oya-ci owns the trusted CI required context. Keep Buck2 authority and do not revive retired CLI or external substrate authority.

queue_policy.reason: High-concurrency dev lanes need a merge queue or equivalent projected-state validation so infra/cloud/product fanout does not serialize all work.

runner_toolchain.fail_closed: rustup toolchain/components/targets, llvm-profdata/llvm-cov, buck2 --version, and Buck2 targets must pass before the shadow evidence succeeds
runner_toolchain.runner_architecture_reason: The current Buck2 Rust toolchain defaults to aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, so the temporary GitHub bridge uses native arm64 runners instead of x64 cross-linking.

github_bridge.required_context_reason: Prow/Kubernetes-native oya-ci posts the trusted oya-ci-required context. GitHub Actions may keep a github-lane-unlocker-required shadow aggregate for compatibility and evidence visibility, but it is not merge authority.

javascript_action_runtime.node26_action_runtime_reason: GitHub JavaScript action runtime migration is Node24; Node26 is available through actions/node-versions for explicit setup-node jobs, but these Buck2/Rust bridge workflows do not run Node application tests.
javascript_action_runtime.stability_policy: Use the stable v6 major tag for checkout and fail closed if GitHub Actions requires a newer JavaScript action runtime.

github_actions_cd_bridge.scope: dry-run and artifact/evidence preparation only; native release-conveyor-like CD owns Kubernetes-native promotion and rollback after oya-ci.

build_test_check_authority.reason: Buck2 remains the build/test/check authority because it models the graph, affected-target fanout, remote/hybrid execution, and cacheable parallel work better than raw Cargo in the monorepo.

pattern_adoption_strategy.rationale: Use proven hyperscaler patterns as reference architecture inputs. Do not copy an upstream product wholesale when the durable Oyatie seam needs Rust-first SCM, Buck2 graph authority, Kubernetes-native execution, cloud workspace resources, and decoupled microservices.

github_public_private_publication.role: Publish and mirror selected public/private repositories, PRs, checks, releases, CODEOWNERS/rulesets, and statuses to GitHub while the native SCM owns durable graph authority.

git_protocol.role: Interoperate with ordinary git clients, GitHub remotes, emergency plain-git workflows, and branch protection checks.

github_actions_status_bridge.role: Expose legacy/shadow GitHub Actions required-context evidence while oya-ci-required remains the desired CI authority.

ci_cd_fit.ci_consumes: rust_prow_oya_ci consumes trusted SCM/controller state and emits ProwJob-style Buck2 workloads plus oya-ci-required status
ci_cd_fit.cd_consumes: release-conveyor-like CD consumes signed build/evidence/release ledger outputs after oya-ci
ci_cd_fit.github_role: PR/publication/status adapter only; not durable SCM or CI authority

cloud_workspace_service.role: Kubernetes-native cloud workspace/resource kernel seam that makes infra/cloud/product lanes independent without leaking workspace internals into product services.

rust_prow_oya_ci.role: Native CI/merge automation seam aligned with Prow/Tide patterns, not a blind Prow clone.
rust_prow_oya_ci.scm_dependency: Consumes trusted native SCM/controller snapshots; does not source gate definitions from candidate PR bytes and does not depend on an oya vcs CLI.

buck2_execution.role: Build/test/check authority with affected target fanout, remote or hybrid execution, and deferred materialization where supported.

llvm_source_based_coverage.role: Modern Rust coverage via rustc -C instrument-coverage and LLVM tools, driven by Buck2 targets instead of Tarpaulin.

release_conveyor_cd.role: Native release-conveyor-like CD destination with Kubernetes-native progressive delivery, policy, evidence, rollback, and audit; GitHub Actions CD remains dry-run bridge only.

cncf_cloud_native.microservice_contract: Each service owns one concern, publishes stable APIs/events, avoids shared mutable internals, and can be tested/promoted independently under Buck2 evidence.

kubernetes_execution.job_model: CI jobs become Kubernetes-native workloads in the durable seam; GitHub Actions is only the interim trigger/executor.
kubernetes_execution.shutdown_model: Use controller scale-to-zero or rollout pause/drain semantics for known workloads; do not blindly delete pods because controllers recreate them and can corrupt evidence.

parallel_lane_model.goal: infra/cloud/product work can progress concurrently without serializing on the native CI/CD/cloud substrate cutover.

product.dependency_boundary: Consumes platform contracts only; must not depend on GitHub, GitHub Actions, native SCM internals, or cloud workspace internals.

cloud_platform.dependency_boundary: Publishes stable resources/APIs/events for product and infra lanes.

scm_ci_cd.dependency_boundary: Owns bridge/native developer substrate without making product delivery wait for full native cutover.

governance.dependency_boundary: Records truth and prevents false readiness claims.

parallel_lane_model.safe_parallelism_rule: Use separate worktrees and PRs for disjoint lane families; shared files require one writer or queued patch integration.

auth_shared_substrate_decoupling.rationale: Separating Cloud auth/shared substrate from Oyatie product auth/shared substrate removes shared schema and runtime edit conflicts while infra/cloud/product lanes fan out. Integration is postponed until the Cloud IdP/resource substrate stabilizes, then product services are deliberately rewritten and rewired to consume it.

cloud_identity_shared.scope: Cloud IdP, workspace identity, resource-kernel identities, cloud control-plane authz, service-to-service cloud substrate identity.

oyatie_product_identity_shared.scope: Product tenant/user/session/auth shared surfaces used by current Oyatie product microservices until Cloud IdP consumption rewrite lands.

integration_backlog: rewrite and rewire Oyatie product services to consume Cloud IdP
retire product-local auth/shared contracts after equivalence and migration evidence

future_work_saving_plan.intent: Save future work by making today's decoupling explicit, adapter-shaped, and reversible instead of letting product/cloud auth contracts drift accidentally.

phases.name: separate-contracts-now
phases.outcome: Cloud auth/shared and Oyatie product auth/shared have separate contract roots, schemas, runtime surfaces, tests, and owners.
phases.saves_work_by: avoiding repeated merge conflicts in shared auth files while lanes fan out

phases.name: thin-compatibility-inventory
phases.outcome: Record equivalent concepts between product auth and Cloud IdP without sharing implementation.
phases.saves_work_by: making future rewrite a mapped migration instead of rediscovery

phases.name: cloud-idp-stabilization
phases.outcome: Cloud IdP/resource substrate has stable API/events, policy, audit, rollback, and migration evidence.
phases.saves_work_by: preventing product rewires against unstable Cloud IdP internals

phases.name: product-adapter-rewrite
phases.outcome: Rewrite and rewire Oyatie products to consume Cloud IdP through adapters/facades, then retire product-local auth/shared surfaces after equivalence tests.
phases.saves_work_by: isolating rewire to adapter boundary and migration tests

reuse_rules: Name equivalent identity concepts now, but do not share code/schema yet.
Keep adapter seams narrow and product-facing.
Do not duplicate business policy once Cloud IdP policy is stable; migrate it deliberately.
Keep Buck2 targets separate but add future cross-contract equivalence tests.
anti_rework_checks: No product lane imports Cloud identity internals before P02.
No Cloud lane edits product auth schema before P02.
No shared auth schema file is introduced during P00/P01.
Future migration PR must include equivalence, rollback, and audit evidence.

alternatives_and_counterarguments.counterargument: Fastest unlock but creates platform lock-in and contradicts native SCM/CI/CD ownership.
Mature Kubernetes CI, but wholesale adoption would keep Go/Prow semantics as authority instead of Oyatie Rust/Buck2/resource contracts.
Sapling provides monorepo ergonomics, but durable Python/C++ control surfaces conflict with the Rust-first native SCM seam.
Maximal control, but high reinvention risk and likely misses Prow/Tide/Piper/CitC/Sapling lessons.
A pure native SCM without GitHub adapters maximizes control but blocks public/private publication, open collaboration, temporary PR interop, and migration safety.
Manual stale-doc sweeps do not scale in a large monorepo and leave confusing active context for agents.

forbidden_claims: GitHub Actions is the permanent CI authority
GitHub Actions is the permanent CD authority
retired external SCM/CI/CD substrates are interim authorities
GitHub Actions shadow checks are CI authority

keep native cutover context separate from GitHub temporary context
defer: delete tracked legacy bridge scripts only after native or GitHub bridge replacement has green evidence

cleanup_policy.doc_sprawl_policy: root docs stay pointer-thin; stale docs older than 3 days are audit/archive candidates; exact retired-substrate names are centralized in /specs/retired-external-substrate-registry.json.
